# TLS test fixtures — not secrets, not for use anywhere else

Everything in this directory is throwaway material for the offline transport
tests in `src/transport.rs` and the config tests in `tests/capabilities.rs`.
It is committed on purpose, and there is nothing here to protect.

| file | what it is |
| --- | --- |
| `ca.pem` | The certificate of a test-only CA (`CN=mu-irc-gateway test CA`). A test feeds it to `[irc] tls_ca_file` to prove that a privately-signed server certificate verifies when its CA is configured, and is refused when it is not. |
| `server.pem` | A leaf certificate signed by that CA, for `CN=irc.test.invalid`, with `subjectAltName = IP:127.0.0.1, DNS:irc.test.invalid`. `.invalid` is reserved by RFC 2606 and never resolves; the loopback SAN is what lets a test server on `127.0.0.1` present it. |
| `server.key.pem` | The private key for `server.pem` (PKCS#8, P-256). The in-process test TLS server needs it to present the leaf. |
| `slot-a.pem`, `slot-b.pem` | Two self-signed CLIENT certificates (`CN=mu-irc-gateway test slot a`/`b`), standing in for the credential a leased slot account presents. Self-signed and CA-less on purpose: a server's certfp matches a fingerprint rather than a chain, so that is the shape a real slot is provisioned with. |
| `slot-a.key.pem`, `slot-b.key.pem` | Their private keys (PKCS#8, P-256). |
| `make-tls-fixtures.sh` | Regenerates all seven. |

**The two slot certificates must stay distinct.** One certificate fingerprint
maps to one account, so a pool that files the same certificate under two slots
is a misconfiguration the config refuses at load — and a test in
`tests/capabilities.rs` proves it by copying one slot's pair over the other.
The generator checks their fingerprints differ before it finishes.

**The CA's private key was never kept.** The generator creates it in a temp
directory, signs the one leaf, and deletes it. Nothing can be signed under
this CA again; possessing `ca.pem` grants trust in exactly one certificate,
for a name that cannot resolve and an address that is always the local host.

**The leaf and slot keys are test-only.** They were generated by the script
and have never protected anything. `server.key.pem` can authenticate nothing
but a test server that a test in this crate starts and tears down, and its
certificate is valid only for `irc.test.invalid` and `127.0.0.1`, so no client
following normal server-name checks would accept it for any real host. The
slot pairs are registered with no server at all — the config tests only load
them from disk — so they identify nothing anywhere.

**None of this may be used outside the test suite.** Do not configure a
gateway, an IRC server, or any other software with these files, and do not
copy them anywhere as a starting point. An operator setting up a private CA
follows the `openssl` recipe in the crate `README.md`, with a CA key they keep.

## Regenerating

The fixtures are committed rather than generated at test time because the
workspace has no certificate-generation crate and the test does not justify
adding one. They are valid for 10 years from generation; to replace them:

```sh
sh crates/mu-irc-gateway/tests/fixtures/make-tls-fixtures.sh
```

The script writes all seven files in place, verifies the chain, and checks
that the two slot certificates do not share a fingerprint. Commit the server
three together — a leaf from one run does not verify under a CA from another.
The slot pairs are self-signed and independent, so they may be regenerated on
their own.
